origin.description: Build the set of functions evaluate calls for source, text, graphics, messages, warnings, errors, and values.
origin.usage: new_output_handler(source = identity, text = identity, graphics = identity, message = identity, warning = identity, error = identity, value = render, calling_handlers = list())

arguments.name: source
arguments.text: Called with each source expression. The default keeps it.

arguments.name: text
arguments.text: Called with each chunk of printed text.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Called with each result. The default prints a visible value.

arguments.name: calling_handlers
arguments.text: Named functions installed while the input is evaluated.

origin.details: A value handler with one argument stores whatever it returns. The default handler prints only a visible value, so print() and cat() are not printed twice.
origin.example:
handler <- new_output_handler(value = function(x) x)
ev <- evaluate("1 + 1", output_handler = handler)
cat("1 + 1 is kept as", ev[[length(ev)]], "\n")

arguments.name: source

translation.details: A value handler with one argument stores whatever it returns. The default handler prints only a visible value, so print() and cat() are not printed twice.
